findings: All 21 global-registry lifecycle cases pass in Chromium 153, Firefox 155 and WebKit 26.6 after explicit registry selection at Lit's public creationScope/importNode boundary; the same 21 pass after Lit compilation.

Baseline passes Chromium/Firefox but WebKit does not upgrade late-defined importNode-created elements and the helper then lacks the target method. A six-route reduced test without house components reproduces the issue in native importNode and ordinary Lit templates; createElement and cloneNode controls upgrade.

Fresh-page registry experiments prevent cross-case contamination: WebKit default import has null registry and fails late upgrade; an explicit registry or initialize fixes it. Chromium passes both; Firefox lacks initialize/scoped registry support in this run.

The modern DOM importNode dictionary uses selfOnly, not deep. The final test uses the standard field. An earlier exploratory script supplied unrecognized deep:true and has been superseded by isolated standard-field checks.
Use the intended registry when creating nodes through supported Lit creationScope; do not hide a generic import/registry problem inside the styling directive or patch global DOM methods.

The tested helper uses AsyncDirective, WeakRef to avoid strongly retaining a discarded directive in a pending whenDefined callback, and generation checks to prevent stale asynchronous writes. Tests verify callback effects, not garbage collection or subscription performance.

Explicit updates to an already-defined element while the Lit part is disconnected still update canonical inputs synchronously; pending late-definition callbacks are suspended/cancelled and reconnect applies current inputs.

Two string-valued inputs and the global registry only. Scoped registries, adopted documents, complete ownership/cleanup policy, concurrent writers, full types, responsive inputs and all styling properties remain open.
No production source, project dependencies, app settings or notes were changed in Plan mode. All owned servers/browser processes are stopped; temporary fixture files/caches remain.

reproduction.notes: Scripts use the previously captured compiled Capturing fixture and dedicated temporary browser cache. Paths/ports describe the probe run and may need to be recreated. Production code was not modified. The isolated registry matrix is authoritative; earlier combined-page exploration is superseded.
